# 1 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_004_page_001.jpg

---

1. Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand picked cavalry, and this detachment moved out by night
2. to fall upon the Judean camp and attack it suddenly, guided by men from the citadel.
3. But Judas learned of it and moved out himself with his warriors to strike the royal forces at Emmaus,
4. while the main force was still away from the camp.
5. When Gorgias entered the camp of Judas by night, he found no one there; so he went searching in the hills, thinking: "These men are fleeing from us."
6. When day was breaking, Judas appeared in the plain with three thousand men, though they lacked the armor and swords they needed.
7. They saw the Gentile camp — well-fortified and strong, with cavalry all around it — trained fighting men.
8. Judas said to his men: "Do not be afraid of their numbers or dread their attack.
9. Remember how our ancestors were saved at the Red Sea when Pharaoh pursued them with his entire force.
10. Let us now cry to Heaven to see whether he will favor us and remember the covenant with our ancestors and crush this army before us today —
11. so that all the Gentiles will know there is one who redeems and saves Israel."
12. The foreigners looked up and saw them coming toward them.
13. They came out of their camp for battle, and the men with Judas sounded the trumpet.
14. They clashed in battle, and the Gentiles broke and fled into the plain.
15. The last of them fell by the sword. They were pursued to Gazara, to the plains of Idumea, Azotus, and Jamnia. About three thousand of them fell.
16. Then Judas and his army turned back from the pursuit.
17. He said to the people: "Do not be greedy for the plunder, for there is still fighting ahead of us.
18. Gorgias and his force are in the hills nearby. Stand your ground against the enemy now and fight them; then afterward take the plunder boldly."
19. Even as Judas was finishing these words, a detachment appeared in the hills coming down to look.
20. They saw that their own force had been put to flight and that the camp was on fire; the rising smoke showed clearly what had happened.
21. When they realized what was happening, they were seized with great fear. When they also saw Judas's army in the plain, drawn up and ready for battle,
22. they all fled to Philistine territory.
23. Then Judas returned to plunder the camp, and they carried off large amounts of gold and silver, blue and purple cloth, and great wealth.
24. On their return they sang a hymn of praise and blessed Heaven, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever.
25. Israel won a great victory that day.
26. Those foreigners who had survived came and reported to Lysias everything that had happened.
27. When he heard, he was dismayed and disheartened, because things had not turned out in Israel the way he had intended, and the outcome was not what the king had commanded.
28. The following year he assembled sixty thousand crack infantry and five thousand cavalry to make war on the Judeans.
29. They came to Idumea and encamped at Beth-zur, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
30. When he saw that the army was strong, he prayed: "Blessed are you, O Savior of Israel, who broke the attack of the mighty warrior by the hand of your servant David, and delivered the camp of the foreigners into the hands of Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer.
31. Hem in this army by the hand of your people Israel; let them be put to shame with all their forces and cavalry.
32. Fill them with dread; cause the confidence of their strength to melt away; let them tremble at their own destruction.
33. Cut them down with the sword of those who love you, and let all who know your name praise you with songs."
34. They joined battle, and about five thousand of Lysias's men fell in close combat before them.
35. When Lysias saw the rout of his forces and the boldness of Judas's troops — how ready they were to live or die with honor — he withdrew to Antioch and began recruiting mercenaries, planning to return to Judah with even larger forces.
36. Then Judas and his brothers said: "Now that our enemies are crushed, let us go up to purify the sanctuary and rededicate it."
37. The whole army mustered and went up to Mount Zion.
38. They found the sanctuary desolate, the altar profaned, the gates burned down, weeds growing in the courts as in a forest or on some mountainside, and the priests' chambers in ruins.
39. They tore their garments and gave way to great lamentation, and sprinkled ashes on their heads,
40. and fell on their faces to the ground. They sounded the signal trumpets and cried out toward Heaven.
41. Then Judas detailed troops to fight the men in the citadel while he purified the sanctuary.
42. He chose priests who were blameless and devoted to the Torah;
43. they purified the sanctuary and carried the stones of the defilement to an unclean place.
44. They deliberated about what to do with the altar of burnt offerings that had been desecrated.
45. The sound decision came to them to tear it down, so that it might not be a disgrace to them, since the Gentiles had defiled it. So they tore it down.
46. They stored the stones in a suitable place on the temple hill, until a prophet should come and give a ruling about them.
47. Then they took uncut stones, as the Torah commands, and built a new altar on the model of the previous one.
48. They rebuilt the sanctuary, the interior of the house, and the courts.
49. They made new sacred vessels and brought the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.
50. They burned incense on the altar and lit the lamps on the lampstand, and the temple was lit up.
51. They set the bread of the Presence on the table, hung the curtains, and completed all the work they had undertaken.
52. On the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-eighth year, they rose early in the morning
53. and offered sacrifice in accordance with the Torah on the new altar of burnt offerings they had built.
54. At the very time and on the very day that the Gentiles had profaned it, it was rededicated with songs, harps, lutes, and cymbals.
55. All the people fell on their faces, worshiped, and blessed Heaven who had brought them success.
56. For eight days they celebrated the dedication of the altar, joyfully offering burnt offerings, offering a sacrifice of well-being and thanksgiving.
57. They decorated the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, restored the gates and the priests' chambers and fitted them with doors.
58. There was very great rejoicing among the people, and the disgrace inflicted by the Gentiles was removed.
59. Judas, his brothers, and the whole assembly of Israel decreed that the days of the rededication of the altar should be observed with joy and gladness at their season, every year for eight days, beginning on the twenty-fifth of Chislev.
60. At that time they also built high walls and strong towers around Mount Zion, so that the Gentiles could not come and trample them down as they had done before.
61. He stationed a garrison there to hold it, and also fortified Beth-zur to guard it, so that the people might have a stronghold facing Idumea.
